label: rem:aeon-remark
title: Aeons as unions of light cones
html:
An aeon \mathcal{A} is a maximal full subcategory of \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ} such that a zigzag of morphisms (flow maps, inclusions, or their inverses) connects any two objects \mathcal{S} and \mathcal{S}' without leaving \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ}. Every light cone forms a directed diagram within the aeon. The aeon unions all light cones that connect without crossing a jet horizon.

Maximality. The connected-component definition guarantees maximality automatically. No larger subcategory of \mathrm{Bun}^{\circ} containing \mathcal{A} is connected. One avoids defining an explicit interval (a, b) \subset \mathbb{Z}. Instead, one defines the aeon over the full categorical structure, naturally encompassing all intersecting light cones.
